title: Documenting Large Webtext Corpora: A Case Study on the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus
measurement_description: Analysis of how a blocklist filter disproportionately removes documents mentioning religious identities (Christian, Jewish, Muslim). Also, measurement of sentiment bias in a language model (UnifiedQA) pretrained on the C4 corpus, specifically evaluating the positivity associated with Jewish vs. Arab identities.
findings: The study found that blocklist filtering in the C4 dataset creation process disproportionately affects documents mentioning minority identities, including religious groups like Jews and Muslims. A downstream analysis of the UnifiedQA model (fine-tuned from T5, which was pretrained on C4) revealed significant sentiment bias; it associated 'Jewish' with a much higher positivity score (67.1%) compared to 'Arab' (37.0%), a bias that was shown to correlate with sentiment expressed in the C4 corpus itself.
